questions.q: What is the difference between GRANT SELECT ANY TABLE and GRANT SELECT ON hr.employees?
options: SELECT ANY TABLE is a schema-crossing system privilege allowing SELECT on every table in the database; SELECT ON hr.employees is an object privilege scoped to just that one table
They are functionally identical
SELECT ANY TABLE only works for the DBA role
SELECT ON hr.employees actually grants broader access than SELECT ANY TABLE
questions.explain: ANY privileges cross every schema in the database, while an object privilege on a specific table is narrowly scoped — the least-privilege choice for someone who only needs one table.

questions.q: What does the CONNECT predefined role actually grant, since Oracle 10g?
options: Essentially just CREATE SESSION — far less than it historically bundled in older Oracle versions
Every system privilege in the database
Full DBA-equivalent access
Nothing at all — CONNECT is deprecated and grants no privileges
questions.explain: CONNECT was reduced to essentially CREATE SESSION since Oracle 10g — a real, worth-knowing gotcha for anyone assuming it does more.

questions.q: What does WITH GRANT OPTION allow, when attached to an object privilege grant?
options: The grantee can turn around and grant that same privilege to someone else
The grantee can never lose the privilege once granted
The privilege automatically expires after 90 days
It has no real effect on the grant
questions.explain: WITH GRANT OPTION lets a user propagate the privilege further, which is worth auditing for sprawl.

questions.q: What does a role let a DBA do that granting privileges one at a time doesn't?
options: Define a bundle of privileges once and assign it to many users, changing the role's privileges in one place instead of chasing individual grants
Roles have no functional benefit over individual grants
Roles can only be granted to exactly one user at a time
Roles bypass Oracle's privilege system entirely
questions.explain: A role is a named collection of privileges — the same 'define once, assign broadly' benefit SQL Server database roles provide.

questions.q: What does the RESOURCE predefined role grant, and what side-effect privilege does it quietly carry?
options: Object-creation privileges (CREATE TABLE, CREATE PROCEDURE, etc.) scoped to the grantee's own schema, plus UNLIMITED TABLESPACE in most releases
Full database-wide administrative access equivalent to SYS
Only the ability to log in, nothing else
Read-only SELECT access to every table
questions.explain: RESOURCE is meant for schema owners building their own objects, but its quiet UNLIMITED TABLESPACE grant is worth knowing before handing it out casually.
